hook_text: One of the first computers filled a whole room and weighed as much as five elephants. Today, a phone is far more powerful.
clip_script: 1946: a giant computer fills a room with cupboards of wires, switches and glowing tubes, and scientists walk between them. Then desk computers with big, heavy screens. Then laptops, tablets and phones. And joining them all, the internet: cables under the sea and signals through the air, linking billions of devices. In 1988, the first email link to the internet in South Africa connected a university in Makhanda to the world.
visual_style: Whiteboard timeline: a room full of computer cabinets, a desktop computer, a laptop and a phone, then a globe with undersea cables landing on the South African coast and lines connecting devices.
mood: Amazed and forward-looking, like peeking into the future.
pacing: Shrink the computers quickly from room-size to pocket-size, then zoom out to the world web of connections.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and talk with an adult about one rule for staying safe online.
